newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's 1997 current account gap to widen - Malan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's 1997 current account gap to widen - Malan.

text.p: Brazil's current account balance of payments deficit will be slightly higher this year compared with 1996, said Finance Minister Pedro Malan.
"The current account deficit will be slightly higher this year," he said.
Brazil showed a current account gap of 2.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1995 and 3.3 percent of GDP in 1996, Malan said.
However, Malan noted that a deficit of 3.0 or 4.0 percent of GDP is not high compared with other countries.
"This percentage is in no way a historic record, without parallel in the world," he told bankers at the swearing-in ceremony of the new president of the Brazilian Association of International Banks.
Malan's comments were a response to questions raised by the association's new chief Bernard Mencier, who expressed market concerns over the deterioration of Brazil's external accounts.
The Finance Minister said that what is important to notice is how the deficit has been financed. He said the financing has been improving significantly as foreign direct investment increases.
"It makes no sense to worry about the trade balance on a daily basis. Whoever follows trade knows that there are enormous fluctuations (in exports and imports) daily," he added.
So far this year Brazil's trade deficit has amounted to $3.057 billion, more than half of last year's $5.5 billion trade gap.
Malan also reinforced the government aims to reach a primary budget surplus of 1.5 percent of GDP this year.
